text:
The snapshot looks like January 2016. The fed funds rate is 0.38%, which fits the period right after the December 2015 hike. Unemployment is 5.0%, and Baa spreads are wide at 3.48 because of the oil and high-yield stress. Industrial production is down 1.75% YoY, the dollar is strong, and the VIX is 22.42. Equities fell 6.6% in the month, the 10-year yield is 2.00%, and emerging-market equities are down 22% over 12 months. That pattern fits January 2016 better than February 2016, when the 10-year was about 1.78%.

Headline CPI at 0.66% YoY and payrolls averaging about 284k over three months also match the late-2015 data.

The 10-year yield at 2.00% suggests end of January 2016, when it was about 1.94%, or possibly end of December 2015, when it was about 2.27%. The 1-month equity return of -6.6% matches January 2016, since the S&P 500 fell about 5%. The December 2015 drop was only about 1.6%, so January is the better fit.
